(CNN) -- Police have arrested a man in the killing of Auburn University freshman Lauren Burk, who died this week, according to the Auburn, Alabama, assistant police chief. Courtney Larrell Lockhart, 23, of Smiths, Alabama, is charged with capital murder during a kidnapping, capital murder during a robbery, and capital murder during an attempted rape, Tommy Dawson said Saturday. The Phenix City Police Department took Lockhart into custody on Friday, police said. Phenix City is about 35 miles southeast of Auburn. Burk, 18, from Marietta, Georgia, was found shot on North College Street, a few miles north of campus, on Tuesday night. She died later at a hospital. Minutes after police responded to the call reporting an injured person and found Burk, they found a car -- which turned out to be Burk's -- on fire in a campus parking lot. Dawson told reporters Friday that authorities think gasoline or another accelerant was used to ignite Burk's car, and police were investigating whether a gas can found in downtown Auburn was connected. Police want to investigate every possible lead, Dawson said. Authorities were still on patrol in the east Alabama campus, he said. The university's Web site said a campus-wide memorial service will be held Monday. The site carried a message from Burk's father, James, which said: "The Burk family was so proud to have Lauren as an Auburn University student. We want to extend our deepest gratitude and appreciation for Auburn University, the city of Auburn and the Auburn Police Department. We feel very close to your community. We appreciate what everyone is doing for us and Lauren." Also on Friday, police released pictures of a 2001 Honda Civic similar to Burk's car. Authorities asked anyone who thinks they might have seen the car on Tuesday to contact them. Police are continuing to interview people, Dawson said. A student at the University of North Carolina in Chapel Hill -- Eve Carson, 22, of Athens, Georgia -- was also shot to death this week, on early Wednesday. Authorities in Chapel Hill said Friday they had been in contact with Auburn police but did not believe the two cases were connected.   Watch CNN's Nancy Grace discuss the two killings of college women from Georgia » . Burk's family, in a statement read Friday to reporters by family friend Kathy Singleton, expressed their gratitude for the thoughts and prayers offered, but asked for privacy "so that they may grieve for their loss as well as celebrate Lauren's life." Those wishing to honor Burk could do so by donating to her favorite charities, Singleton said -- The Invisible Child and the American Kidney Foundation. Donations can be made at any Wachovia Bank to the Lauren Burk Memorial Fund. E-mail to a friend .

Courtney Larrell Lockhart, 23, of Smiths, Alabama, has been charged with capital murder during a kidnapping, capital murder during a robbery, and capital murder during an attempted rape, Assistant Police Chief Tommy Dawson announced on Saturday. According to police, the Phenix City Police Department took Lockhart into custody on Friday. Phenix City lies approximately 35 miles southeast of Auburn.

Burk, 18, of Marietta, Georgia, was discovered with a gunshot wound on North College Street, a few miles north of campus, on Tuesday night. She later succumbed to her injuries at a local hospital. Only minutes after responding to a call reporting an injured person and locating Burk, officers found a car engulfed in flames in a campus parking lot—which was subsequently identified as belonging to Burk.

Dawson told reporters on Friday that authorities believe gasoline or another accelerant was used to ignite Burk's vehicle, and that investigators were examining whether a gas can recovered in downtown Auburn was connected to the incident. Dawson emphasized that police intended to pursue every possible lead, adding that authorities remained on patrol throughout the east Alabama campus.

According to the university's website, a campus-wide memorial service will be held on Monday. The site also featured a message from Burk's father, James, which read: "The Burk family was so proud to have Lauren as an Auburn University student. We want to extend our deepest gratitude and appreciation for Auburn University, the city of Auburn and the Auburn Police Department. We feel very close to your community. We appreciate what everyone is doing for us and Lauren."

Also on Friday, police released photographs of a 2001 Honda Civic similar to Burk's car, urging anyone who may have seen the vehicle on Tuesday to come forward. Dawson noted that police were continuing to interview individuals as part of the investigation.

In a separate incident this week, a student at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill—Eve Carson, 22, of Athens, Georgia—was also fatally shot in the early hours of Wednesday. Authorities in Chapel Hill said on Friday that, although they had been in contact with Auburn police, they did not believe the two cases were connected. On Saturday, Tommy Dawson identified the suspect as 23-year-old Courtney Larrell Lockhart from Smiths, Alabama, who now faces three counts of capital murder—one occurring during a kidnapping, another during a robbery, and a third during an attempted rape.

According to police, Lockhart was arrested Friday by officers from the Phenix City Police Department, a town located roughly 35 miles to the southeast of Auburn.

The 18-year-old victim, who came from Marietta, Georgia, was discovered with gunshot wounds on North College Street, situated several miles north of the university campus, on Tuesday evening. She was later taken to a hospital, where she passed away.

Just moments after officers arrived in response to a call about an injured individual and located Burk, they discovered a vehicle engulfed in flames in a campus parking lot. That car was later identified as belonging to Burk.

During a Friday briefing, Dawson explained that investigators believe gasoline or some other flammable substance was used to set the car ablaze, and that police were looking into whether a gas can discovered in downtown Auburn had any link to the crime. He stressed that officials intended to pursue every potential lead and noted that patrols were still active on the east Alabama campus.

The university announced on its website that a memorial service open to the entire campus would take place Monday. On Friday, investigators also made public images of a 2001 Honda Civic resembling the one Burk owned. They urged anyone who may have spotted such a vehicle on Tuesday to reach out to them. Dawson added that officers were still conducting interviews.

Officials in Chapel Hill stated Friday that although they had communicated with Auburn police, they did not think the two killings were related.

In a statement delivered to reporters on Friday by family friend Kathy Singleton, Burk's relatives thanked everyone for the thoughts and prayers they had received but requested privacy "so that they may grieve for their loss as well as celebrate Lauren's life."
